## [0.21.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.20.1...v0.21.0) (2026-11-23)
Publish your encryption key and find other people's, and sender checks that a forged message can no longer fool.
### Features
* **Publish your key.** Encryption Keys > Publish puts your public key on keys.openpgp.org so others can find it by your address. The server sends a confirmation link to each address not yet listed; an address is listed only once you open its link. * **Find Key.** A message signed with a key you do not have offers Find Key beside its label: the key is looked up by its fingerprint, and the label then names who signed it. Contact Properties has Find Key for a contact without a usable key, and Encrypt looks up recipients' keys by itself, first at the address's own domain, then on keys.openpgp.org (which can be turned off in Reading settings). * **Import from Clipboard** in Encryption Keys adds a key copied as text, and **Import Key** on a key attached to a message adds it from the message. Keys that come in mail are taken as public keys only. * **The Address Book marks contacts who have a key**, with a stronger mark for keys you have verified. * **Trust sender checks from**, in Account Properties, names the servers whose checks on senders the account believes. It is filled in for well-known providers (with every regional Zoho server), and you can add your own server's name if it writes its checks under another one.
### Bug Fixes
* **Sender checks only believe your own provider's newest verdict**, the one your mail server writes on top of the message. A sender could write a verdict of their own lower down; at Zoho, which keeps such headers and whose own verdicts the app did not recognise, a forged message could show as a confirmed sender, offer a sign-in code card or show a brand logo. Messages from the last 90 days are checked again in the background after the update. * **More real senders are confirmed.** Mail from a subdomain of a confirmed domain (such as news.shop.com for shop.com) now counts, as do Gmail, Yahoo and GMX verdicts that name the signer only by its address, and verdicts with comments inside them (as some self-hosted servers write). * **Brand logos need the provider's own logo check**, aligned with the sender, and a certified mark where the provider reports one.

## [0.20.1](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.19.1...v0.20.1) (2026-11-22)
Six new languages, a mailing-list bar for unsubscribing, and search that finds words written without spaces.
### Features
* **Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, Indonesian and Vietnamese.** The windows, the menus and the help in each, reviewed. Chinese follows your system: Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau get Traditional Chinese, other regions Simplified. On Windows, Japanese, Chinese and Korean are drawn in the font Windows itself uses for them. * **Search finds Chinese, Japanese and Korean words** inside a subject or message, though these languages write no spaces between words. Replies and forwards recognise their reply prefixes (回复, 返信, 회신, 转发 and others), so a subject no longer collects "Re: 回复:". * **A mailing-list bar replaces the Unsubscribe link.** A message from a list shows a bar naming the list, with an Unsubscribe button. Unsubscribe from List is also in the Message menu and on a message's right-click menu. After you unsubscribe, the bar says when you asked, and tells you if the list keeps writing more than two days later. * **The other actions that looked like links are now buttons**: Download Pictures, Try Again, Create Rule and Clear search, and the setup buttons of Add Mail Account and AI Agents. * **A folder opens with a message.** Coming back to a folder shows the message you left it on, a folder opened for the first time shows its newest message, and the app starts in the folder it was closed in. * **Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 mail gets sign-in code cards, one-click Unsubscribe, brand logos and confirmed senders.** Microsoft gives its verdict on a sender in a different header from other providers, which the app now reads. * **Flag changes are not lost.** Read, flagged, colours and junk marks made offline, or while a connection failed, reach the server on the next Send/Recv.
### Bug Fixes
* **Typing Chinese, Japanese or Korean:** on the Mac, the search box no longer searches text you are still composing; on Linux, Enter in an address field confirms the composition instead of picking an address. * **On Windows, message boxes' buttons (Yes, No, OK, Cancel) are in the app's language,** not in Windows' own. * **Undo brings back every copy of a message moved together,** such as one delivered both by a mailing list and as a Cc. * **Undo and Mark All Read work on more than 1000 messages** with servers that limit how many one command may touch, and selecting thousands of separate messages no longer fails. * **Lists stay where you scrolled them** when they are read again after new mail, and a click while a list is being read is no longer lost. * **On Linux, rows drawn while scrolling quickly are filled in**, a row selected while still blank keeps its message, and a draft always opens. * **Unsubscribe by mail from a message window** writes from that message's account, on the Mac and Linux.

## [0.19.1](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.19.0...v0.19.1) (2026-11-19)
Two fixes for 0.19.0.
### Bug Fixes
* **On Linux, a large folder's list no longer goes blank.** In a folder of more than 800 messages, choosing another folder and coming back, or a sync in the background, could leave the list's rows empty, and a row selected opened nothing. * **On the Mac, the Tools menu now has Message Rules and Encryption Keys, and the Message menu has Create Rule from Message.** They were missing from the menu bar, so rules and keys, such as importing a key you already have, could not be reached there.
